'''Arata Shrine''' (Arata-jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Mori, {{ill|Iwade, Wakayama|Q579623|qid=Q579623}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
The ancient origins are unknown. In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}} lists “Arata Shrine, two seats” in {{ill|Naga District, Wakayama|Q1093809|qid=Q1093809|lt=Naga District}}, {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}, placing it among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. The {{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}} records it as a local deity with the rank “Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade, Arata-no-Kami.”

According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}} (an Edo-period gazetteer of Kii Province), the enshrined deities were {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto}}, the ancestor of the Arata no Atae clan, and {{ill|Katsuragi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|葛城国造|qid=Q11620893|lt=Tsurugine-no-Mikoto}}, and later—like {{ill|Hirota Shrine (Osaka City)|Q1466105|qid=Q1466105}} in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}—{{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫|zh|瀨織津姬神|qid=Q13579836|lt=Ama-no-Somukitsu-Hime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}} were added<ref name="place-names"/>. Because this {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ama-no-Somukitsu-Hime-no-Mikoto}} is considered the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aramitama}} of {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, it is thought that Arata Shrine originated from {{ill|Kōjin|Q6455190|qid=Q6455190|lt=aragami worship}}<ref name="place-names">“Place Names of Wakayama Prefecture,” entry for Arata Shrine.</ref>. The same source states that the shrine was destroyed by warfare during the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}–{{ill|1592|Q6769|qid=Q6769}})<ref name="place-names"/>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period, under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Divine rank ===
* Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}) — recorded as “Arata-no-Kami.”

=== Shrine grounds ===
[[File:Arata-jinja (Iwade) keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sacred grove and worship hall within the grounds}}]]
The main hall was rebuilt in the first year of {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} ({{ill|1624|Q6821|qid=Q6821}}). It is a sangensha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with a {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} roof. The entire structure is vermilion-lacquered and adorned with carvings said to have been donated by {{ill|Heinouchi Masanobu|Q11482097|qid=Q11482097|lt=Heiuchi Masanobu}}. This main hall is designated a {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860|lt=Prefectural Tangible Cultural Property}} of {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}.

=== Subsidiary and auxiliary shrines ===
* Inari Shrine — enshrined deities: {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q276944}}
* Niu Shrine
* Yasaka Shrine

=== Festivals ===
* New Year’s Day Festival (January 1)<ref>Festival information is based on the explanatory leaflet within the shrine grounds.</ref>
* Spring Festival (February 19)
* Ohatsuho (June 30)
* Gion Festival (July 7)
* Summer Festival (August 19)
* Tanomo Festival (August 31)
* Autumn Festival (October 5)
* Shichi-Go-San pilgrimage (early November)
* Ohatsuho (November 24)
* Ohitaki (late December)

In addition, there is a special ritual called the New Year Suzu-tamari ritual<ref>[Arata Shrine] (Wakayama Prefecture Shrine Association).</ref>.
